title: Frontend: Nested Comments
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Nested Comments. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Start with comment {id:1,text:Root,parent:null}. Text input + Add[data-action=add] adds trimmed nonblank comment as root or under the last Reply[data-reply=ID] selection. Sequential IDs start 2. Render li[data-comment=ID] nested by parent, text span[data-text=ID]. Delete[data-delete=ID] tombstones text to [deleted], retains descendants, and disables Reply on that node. Blank adds nothing.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Normalize comments by ID with parent IDs and ordered child lists, or use a carefully immutable tree.
alternativeApproaches: Add optimistic replies with temporary IDs and reconcile server acknowledgements without duplicating the thread.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Reply to deleted comment; deep nesting; duplicate text.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
